## RCHIVE is a desktop app for cataloging, searching and reorganizing the files on your computers and drives

It's made for people with more storage than they can keep track of, and it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux

- Old backups
- External drives
- Camera cards
- Network folders
- Thumb drives
- The laptop before this one

## You saved the damn file... why can't you find it again?

You remember the document. You remember working on it. Apparently you also need to remember which computer you used, what you called the folder, and which backup of that computer is on which drive.

RCHIVE keeps a searchable catalog of every folder and drive you add — search a name, see a preview, and find out where the original lives, even if that drive is collecting dust in a drawer somewhere.

## What it actually does

### It finds the file, including the one on that old drive in the attic

Scan a drive once and RCHIVE remembers what's on it: names, folders, dates, and a small preview. Unplug the drive, put it away, and search it anyway. When you find what you're after, RCHIVE tells you which drive to go dig out.

How offline search works →

Pause video

Old Laptop is unplugged — its files still show up, with saved previews and the drive to go get out of storage

### It finds the file when you don't remember what you called it

Search by what you do know: how big it is, when and where it was taken, which camera took it, how wide the picture is, or who's singing. Each filter narrows every drive at once, including the ones in a drawer.

Combine as many as you like. RCHIVE describes the search in plain words, and you can type it out too, with AND, OR and NOT.

Pause video

Every Canon photo, narrowed to the full-size originals

### It sorts the mess, and shows you before it touches anything

Organize My Computer takes forty folders called `misc` and turns them into Photos, Videos, Music, Documents and the rest, by year, camera, album, or whatever fits.

That's a view inside RCHIVE. Your real folders stay exactly as they are until you tell RCHIVE to copy.

![The same catalog under Organize My Computer: Archives, Audio, Documents, Images, Music, Other Files, Photos, Software and Technical, and Videos.](https://www.rchive.computer/assets/reels/organize-after-1600.964cc47a4e.webp)![RCHIVE File Browser showing four drives as their original, deeply nested folders.](https://www.rchive.computer/assets/reels/organize-before-1600.df873c0906.webp) Original folders Organize My Computer

Compare original folders with Organize My Computer

Drag to compare — same catalog, same window. The folders on disk never moved.

### It knows when your photos were actually taken

Your old backup stamped ten years of photos with the day you ran the backup. RCHIVE reads the date the camera wrote into each photo instead, and when a file doesn't say, it checks the photos around it.

![The same 99 photos by Actual Date: eleven years from 2015 to 2025. The selected photo is back in December 2019, the date its Canon camera recorded.](https://www.rchive.computer/assets/reels/dates-after-1600.6b36190ec6.webp)![RCHIVE sorting 99 photos by file date: all of them fall under 2026, March, the night of the backup. The selected photo shows a date of March 2, 2026.](https://www.rchive.computer/assets/reels/dates-before-1600.0f77b26068.webp) File date Actual Date

Compare file dates with Actual Dates

Drag to compare — the same 99 photos — only “Use Actual Dates” changed

### It knows where your photos were taken

New in RCHIVE 1.2 — Find photos and videos with saved GPS in Hawaii, in New York, or within twenty miles of a point. Search the drives you’ve cataloged, including backups that are unplugged.

RCHIVE looks up places on your computer using data built into the app.

Pause video

Finding cataloged photos with GPS within 30 miles of Hilo

### A long copy shouldn't need a babysitter

Big copies in Explorer and Finder like to die at 97% and leave you guessing which files made it. RCHIVE writes down its progress as it goes.

Pause it, close the laptop, trip over the power cord, and come back Tuesday. It picks up where it stopped, and it can check every copied file against the original.

Pause video

Paused, restarted and resumed, with every copy checked against its original.

## Got questions? Here are some answers

Will organizing change my original files?

Changing recipes, groupings and tags changes the view in RCHIVE. Your files stay in place until you explicitly run a copy or move job. Choose Copy when you want to keep your originals.

Can I search a drive that isn’t plugged in?

Yes, once it has been cataloged. RCHIVE keeps recorded filenames, locations, metadata, and any saved previews. Reconnect the drive to open, copy or make new previews of the originals.

Where should I start?

Add a familiar folder or drive and let RCHIVE scan it. Try Find Anything or Organize My Computer, explore the results, then copy a small selection when you’re ready.

What does the lifetime license include?

One person can activate RCHIVE on up to three devices. All current and future versions and features are included, with no paid upgrades. You can activate online with a key or offline with a license file.

Can I use RCHIVE on more than one operating system?

Yes. Use the compatible Windows, macOS or Linux build for each computer. The download section above and the full download page show what's available for each system.

Does RCHIVE upload anything or process in the cloud?

No — everything RCHIVE learns is stored in its own data folder on your computer, and all operations are performed via code running on your machine.

Does RCHIVE use AI?

No — all operations and decision-making in RCHIVE are deterministic. We're dealing with your files, after all!

Future versions might include local ML-based classifier models, OCR, that sort of thing, but care will be taken to ensure that all decision-making is repeatable, predictable, reliable, and able to be audited.
